title: Anonymous article feedback uniqueness is ineffective on SQLite

evidence.quote: user_id: UUID | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="users.id", index=True)

reasoning: The model permits null user_id values while relying on a composite unique constraint over user_id and article_id. SQLite allows multiple NULL values in a unique constraint, so unauthenticated/global feedback for the same article can be duplicated instead of upserted, especially under concurrent requests.
reproduction: Insert two ArticleFeedback rows with the same article_id and user_id=None; SQLite accepts both rows despite the declared unique constraint.
recommendation: Make user_id non-null for feedback rows, or add a generated/sentinel user key for anonymous feedback and enforce uniqueness on that normalized key plus article_id. If anonymous feedback must stay nullable, add application-level transaction handling plus a SQLite-compatible unique index strategy.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The inspected feedback roundtrip test covers a single create/delete path and does not attempt duplicate anonymous inserts or concurrent upserts.
suggestedRegressionTest: Against SQLite, insert or upsert the same article feedback twice with user_id=None and assert the table still contains exactly one row.
minimumFixScope: ArticleFeedback schema, feedback upsert logic, and an Alembic migration/index strategy compatible with existing data.
